title: Photo survey
description: Ground-level photographic observations used to inform and promote a module's appearance data. Deliberately an EVIDENCE contract, not an image gallery: each record ties a photograph to a place, a direction, a moment and a licence, and states which assets it observes. That is what lets a photo raise a facade from an inferred grade C to an observed grade B, and what stops an unlicensed or undated image being used to do so. See PHOTO-SURVEY.md.

campaign.description: The collection effort these observations belong to.

position.description: Where the camera stood. Geodetic from EXIF GPS, or scene-space once resolved, or an address geocode.

position_source.description: How the position was obtained. Drives position_accuracy_m and the confidence an observation can grant.

position_accuracy_m.description: Radius of uncertainty. Consumer-phone GPS in a street canyon is commonly 10-30 m, which is worse than the width of the street; that is why bearing and subject reference matter more than position alone.

bearing_deg.description: Compass direction the camera faced, degrees clockwise from true north. Without this a photo says what a place looks like but not from where, and cannot be used to observe a specific facade.

hfov_deg.description: Horizontal field of view, from EXIF focal length and sensor size where available.

captured_at.description: When the photograph was taken, NOT when it was uploaded. Required for anything claiming to describe current conditions. Truncated forms are legal and preferred over invention: an image known only to its year is '1898', a decade is '1890s'. A full timestamp must never be manufactured to satisfy a format, because the padding would read as knowledge nobody has - state captured_precision and let the string be as short as the evidence.

captured_precision.description: How precisely captured_at is known. An archival photo dated only to a decade is still useful, but must not be presented as current.

observes.description: Assets this photograph shows well enough to inform. An observation with no subjects is context, not evidence.

items.description: What the photograph is good evidence FOR. A wide streetscape may evidence paving and tree size while being useless for one building's window pattern.

quality.description: Fitness for purpose. Recorded rather than inferred at render time so a reviewer can filter before anything is derived.

obstruction.description: Scaffolding matters especially: it hides the very facade the photo was taken for.

rectified.description: True when perspective has been corrected so the facade is fronto-parallel, which is what makes a photo usable as a texture rather than only as reference.

sky_fraction.description: Fraction of the top of the frame that reads as sky. Recorded as a measurement, NOT as an interior/exterior test: measured across a real corpus, interiors scored 0.16 to 0.79 and exteriors 0.51 to 1.00, because rooms with large windows are bright and blue at the top of frame too. Any threshold that rejected the interiors also rejected good street views. Publish the number; leave the judgement to review.

license.description: SPDX identifier or short name. REQUIRED. An image whose licence is unknown cannot be used, however good it is.

attribution_text.description: Credit line to display wherever anything derived from this image is shown.

usage.description: reference_only: a human may look at it, nothing may be derived and it is never published. derive_appearance: colours, materials and dimensions may be derived, the image itself is not redistributed. redistribute: the image may be served to end users.

contains_people.description: Flag for review. Faces and readable plates should be blurred before any image is published.

contributor.description: Who supplied it. Pseudonymous by default: a campaign should never require a contributor's real identity.

source_collection.description: Where a found image came from, e.g. 'Mapillary', 'Wikimedia Commons', 'NYC Municipal Archives'.

category.description: Primary subject, for consumers that want a single label. The first entry of `categories`.

categories.description: Everything a reviewer said the photograph shows. Coarser than `observes[].aspect` and answering a different question: aspect says what may be derived, category says what the picture is OF. A list because one frame usually contains several — a street view is a facade, a pavement and a street tree at once — and tagging it once per subject is what lets each inform only its own thing. Permissions are the union, which makes the awkward combinations fall out for free: `bridge` contributes nothing, so `[bridge, facade]` yields exactly the facade. `historic` is the exception, contributing aspects but never a measured colour, because an archival wall may have been repainted twice since.

grants_confidence.description: Highest confidence an asset aspect derived from this observation may claim. A dated archival photo may grant C; a sharp, well-located, recent, rectified photo may grant B. Photographs alone never grant A.

supersedes.description: observation_id this replaces, e.g. a current photo replacing a dated one of the same subject.

allOf.description: A camera position may be absent, but only when the record SAYS it is unknown. Absence must be declared, never accidental: a harvested archival photograph legitimately has no position, whereas a phone survey that silently dropped its GPS is a defect. Requiring position_source to be present and 'unknown' distinguishes the two.

Stated precision may not exceed what the timestamp actually carries. This is the failure mode worth encoding: a harvester that truncates free text to ten characters and labels every record 'day' produces a corpus that looks precisely dated and is not. A day-precise claim must show a full date; an exact claim must show a time.
